records.KeyDecisions: The approach to build the data model to accommodate the uses cases was to begin with the Academic Advising model, then source published standards for applicable content. The first standard used was always CEDS but other published standards were also used. When no standard aligned with the required data, new objects and columns were created. The vast majority of objects/columns were created either due to the absence of unique column naming and/or column usage and meaning conflicts.

Standards column names were unique within an organization but were not always unique when merged with other standards. In these cases, column names were adjusted to be unique, and attempts to maintain the description, use, and enumerations were made. The source category represents columns that were completely created or modified from a published standard.

The data model supports multi-tenancy. For a multi-tenant implementation, both the organization and person identifier must be constructed in such a way as to ensure unique identifiers. Each table contains a primary key for organization and or person to represent the author and/or the learner about which the data describes.

Organization identifiers that are meaningful in an external or local namespace are stored in OrganizationIdentification and resolved through OrganizationIdentificationSystem. Person alternate identifiers remain separate from canonical PersonIdentifier. Source-system record identities remain source lineage and must not be substituted for canonical identifiers. Matching/crosswalk processes should reconcile incoming source identities to the tenant-scoped canonical records.

A relational approach for designing tables was utilized. Therefore many lookup tables were defined to reduce duplication of data. Likewise, association tables were used to connect data from lookups tables. Although the objects are not in full normal form, the duplication was reduced as much as possible.
All objects contain columns to represent an audit of data. Each include created, updated, and deleted person identifiers with corresponding date columns.
Object and column names were defined in title case to reflect the more common styles.

For crosswalk objects that connect one object type to another, we chose to name them in the format "Object1Object2Association" to be in alignment with LIF and as this seemed cleaner than alternatives like "Object1ToObject2".
SharingPermissions table should act as a running log and updates and deletes should not happen to it.

Lookup tables are used to store predefined data in order to have a single standardized place to retrieve it from using an identifier. These are used to hold data that is a static definition or enumerations. Lookup tables have the naming convention of "{Object}Lookup".
Each table has a primary key column that follows the naming convention "{Object}Identifier" that can be used to uniquely identify the record (row) as well as to reference this row from other tables.

{Object}EducationAssociation tables were created when an object needed to be associated to one or more Education items, such as Assessment, Class, Course, etc. so that the name would not need to be {Object}AssessmentClassCourseTermAssociation.

Naming convention update: the former OrganizationAlternateId and OrganizationIdSystem names are retired. Use OrganizationIdentification and OrganizationIdentificationSystem. Existing person identifier objects retain their established names unless separately refactored.
All column names ending in Identifier should either be referring to a specific primary key or "ObjectIdentifier" which generically refers to a primary key.

"MatchingAttribute" refers to trying to match a course by a given requirement. "Tag" is used to refer to search criteria for the object. When using tags, the tags should have their own table and an association table to the object.
Tracking revisions or changes of unique objects is handled by using an {Object}RevisionIdentifier as an additional primary key and an {Object}RevisionStatus field to track the status of the revision.
All boolean fields should be worded such that the default value is False, if applicable.
Enumerations should not be used to prevent data loss. Enumerations from source standards and research were documented for potential future consideration.
Boolean fields should have the format {Field}Indicator.
When column names include "URL" or "URI", the abbreviation should be entirely capitalized in the name (e.g. URL).
The column name for each table's primary key should be unique to that table.
All tables should always have a PK that is not also FK.
Guideline: The foreign keys in Association tables should be both PK, FK.
For standards that utilized Yes/No enumerations, we converted the data type to boolean.
Object names are only prepended when it adds meaning to distinguish columns within the object.
Guideline: In general, table names should be reflective of the intent of what a single row of data will contain regarding singular or plural objects.
When indicating what order in a sequence an object is, the column for doing this should have the suffix "SequenceNumber".
The suffix referring to a begin, start, or effective date should always be "StartDate".
The suffix referring to a end or expiration should always be "EndDate".
When referring generically to any object of the data model, when naming a column, use the term "Object" to refer to it (not "Item" or "Resource").
When referring generically to the name or title of something, it should be written as Name. When referring to the short name of something, it should be written as ShortName.
Columns for Name and ShortName should all have the description "A name for the record" or "A short name for the record", respectively.
If there is 1 or fewer sentences, then no period at the end of the Description. If it is more than one sentence, then each sentence should have a period at the end of the Description.
When including examples in a Description, use the format "(e.g. value1, value2, etc.)".
Check for spelling errors in column names.
Change objects ending in Detail to Details for future proofing for when more than one thing may exist in these objects down the road.
Detail should be Details in primary key name when the object ends in Details.

Objects with the "Association" suffix will not have InformationSourceOrganizationIdentifier as the information source would be indicated on the associated object lookups themselves.

TenantIdentifier is the tenant data-ownership/security boundary and appears on tenant-owned operational tables. OrganizationIdentifier identifies a real-world organization represented within that tenant and must not be used as the tenant boundary.
PersonIdentifier is tenant-scoped and should be interpreted with TenantIdentifier rather than as a global person key.
PersonIdentifier does not need to be a GUID; readable tenant-scoped surrogate keys remain acceptable.
Cross-organization enrollment should use explicit home and host organization context without creating a global identity pool.
SourceSystemIdentifier and related lineage columns should be included when rows are source-originated, reconciled, or traceable, not blindly on every table.
SourceRaw columns should preserve ambiguous or lossy source-system values alongside canonical values.
New lookup table names should end with Lookup when a dedicated lookup table is justified.
Boolean-style fields should use the Indicator suffix and date-bearing fields should generally use Date.
Child, history, and detail tables may use TenantIdentifier plus parent identifier plus SequenceNumber as a clear tenant-safe key pattern.
Dedicated lookup tables should be reserved for core domain concepts that are heavily referenced or likely to need concept-specific governance.
Narrow lists, reasons, statuses, lightweight types, and dropdown values should generally use Core ReferenceData infrastructure.
ReferenceCodeSet and ReferenceCodeValue belong under Core.ReferenceData, not inside each consuming domain.
Admissions-specific reference code sets should be defined as values in shared reference infrastructure rather than as many small Admissions lookup tables.
ReferenceCodeValue may include limited action-code columns for source-style control behavior without overbuilding lookup tables.
LearnerApplication should remain the table name because Application alone is too generic across higher education.
LearnerApplication should be a lean application header, not a catch-all admissions table.
ApplicationStatusReasonIdentifier should reference ReferenceCodeValue in ReferenceCodeSetCode APPLICATION_STATUS_REASON.
Withdrawal should use a hybrid pattern: summary fields on LearnerApplication, status movement in status history, and detail in LearnerApplicationWithdrawal.
Milestones should be modeled as application events rather than as a separate LearnerApplicationMilestone table.
Status means operational workflow state, decision means formal institutional outcome, and event means notable dated occurrence.
LearnerApplicationDecision is the formal admissions outcome table and should not absorb review-board workflow metadata.
LearnerApplicationProgramInterest records applicant-stated program interests and remains distinct from decision program and enrolled academic program.
LearnerApplicationEvent should be bounded to application timeline support and should not become a catch-all event table.
When an occurrence appears in both a durable application table and LearnerApplicationEvent, the durable table is authoritative.
LearnerApplicationFee records admissions-operational fee obligation and satisfaction while Finance remains authoritative for receivables and accounting.
LearnerApplicationEvent may support response timeline milestones but should not be authoritative for structured applicant response facts.
LearnerApplicationReview is for admissions review/evaluation workflow facts separate from formal decision outcomes.
PersonCitizenship belongs under Person.Demographic as a repeatable person-country citizenship relationship table.
PersonCitizenship should not be folded into PersonDemographics, PersonAddress, PersonResidency, or Admissions-specific structures.
PersonImmigrationStatus belongs under Person.Demographic as the preferred home for visa, permit, immigration, and authorization facts.
PersonRelatedContact should store relevant family/support context without creating a full family-person registry or related-person identity layer.
Within PersonRelatedContact, concise local names should be used where context is clear, with ContactName preferred over bare Name.
ContactTypeIdentifier, RelationshipTypeIdentifier, ContactRoleIdentifier, and ContactPriorityNumber should remain semantically separate.
PersonRelatedContact reference values should use Core.ReferenceData rather than dedicated Person.Relationship lookup tables.
ApplicationSourceIdentifier should not be overloaded with campaign, UTM, funnel, source-code history, territory, or event attribution values.
Communication consent, contact-point attributes, deliverability events, and message history should remain separate concepts.
LearnerThirdPartyBenefit belongs under Finances > LearnerFinances for employer reimbursement, sponsorship, voucher, or outside education-benefit facts.
LearnerThirdPartyBenefit should not be forced into LearnerEmployment, LearnerApplicationFeeWaiver, or detailed Finance transaction tables.
Columns CreatedDate, UpdatedDate, and Deleted date are of type Datetime instead of Date to provide greater precision.

The data model treats advising and care-team assignments as general person-to-person support relationships rather than caseloads. The support role is recorded separately from staff specialty, and whether the assignment is current comes from EffectiveStartDate and EffectiveEndDate. PrimaryAssignmentIndicator means primary within that support role or context, not primary for the staff member overall.

The data model separates the enduring ProgramOfStudy from the specific ProgramCurriculum used to evaluate a learner. A program can remain the same while its requirements change. Requirements belong to the curriculum, and the data model allows the resulting progress to be recorded without trying to reproduce an institution’s degree-audit rules.

The data model separates academic evidence from the institution’s decision to award credit. LearnerAcademicCredit represents credit the institution has actually recognized, while the grade, transfer work, test result, or prior-learning evaluation that led to that credit remains separate. This preserves where the credit came from without treating every source fact as awarded credit.

The data model accounts for degree progress, but avoids reproducing the engine that produced it. Overall program progress, individual requirements, and the evidence used to satisfy those requirements are kept distinct. Requirement-level credits cannot simply be added together because the same credit may satisfy more than one requirement.
The data model distinguishes general person achievements from academic honors and credential honors. Academic honors and credential honors remain tied to their specific academic contexts.

The data model distinguishes 'administrative periods' from academic terms. An administrative period may be used for reporting, residency, cohorts, student types, etc., and may overlap with a term, but it is not necessarily the same thing.

An enduring campus organization is recorded as an Organization, not as a product-specific activity or special-purpose object. Organization type/classification, person membership, and organization hierarchy are represented separately rather than built into the organization itself.

External education is modeled as a lean person-level prior-education fact under Academics.Transfer, with repeating disciplines and academic honors represented by child associations. Externally awarded credential names and performance measures remain source-representational rather than being forced into tenant-governed credential or grading vocabularies.

The data model distinguishes an official course-attempt outcome from the history of changes to that outcome. Grade changes are preserved rather than overwriting earlier results, and official academic outcomes remain separate from LMS-reported grading information. For example, the later model explicitly replaced the provisional EnrollmentAcademicOutcome / LearnerFinalGradeResult design with LearnerCourseAttemptOutcome.

The data model treats educational institutions as organizations within a tenant, not as the tenant itself. TenantIdentifier replaced the earlier use of OrganizationIdentifier as the tenant/security boundary, while OrganizationIdentifier now identifies a real-world organization within that tenant. Institution identity, relationships, classifications, and identifiers are modeled separately so a tenant can represent its own institution as well as schools, employers, agencies, accreditors, and other organizations.
OrganizationLookup replaced by Organization: Core.Organization.Organization is a master entity, not a lookup.
Organization identifications normalized: OrganizationAlternateId and OrganizationIdSystem are replaced by OrganizationIdentification and OrganizationIdentificationSystem.

Organization relationships are first-class: ParentOrganizationIdentifier and RelationshipType were removed from Organization. OrganizationRelationship represents effective-dated typed relationships between organizations, allowing multiple simultaneous relationships rather than forcing a single parent tree.

Tenant-relative organization roles: TenantOrganizationRole represents contextual roles such as HomeInstitution. Employer, accreditor, issuer, recruiter, and similar roles should normally be expressed by the relevant domain relationship rather than as intrinsic organization types.

Semantic grain invariant: when a required parent relationship already determines an ancestral identifier, child objects do not repeat that identifier merely for convenience. Such redundancy creates contradictory-state risk and is removed unless the child fact has an independent semantic need for the identifier.

Program-to-credential relationship consolidated: ProgramCredential is the canonical relationship between ProgramOfStudyLookup and CredentialLookup. CredentialProgramOfStudyAssociation was retired as a semantic duplicate. PersonProgramCredential remains distinct because it represents a learner-specific intended or selected credential outcome, not the program definition itself.

The data model avoids catch-all organization “profile” objects that mix unrelated kinds of information. Stable organization attributes, accreditation, classifications, reporting metrics, and other context-specific facts are modeled separately at their natural grain.

Organization accreditation is first-class: OrganizationAccreditation represents an organization accreditation and references the accrediting agency as another Organization. Accreditation status and lifecycle dates belong to the accreditation relationship, not Organization itself.

OrganizationIndustryCode retired in v0.3.15. NAICS, SIC, ISIC, and comparable industry assignments are organization classifications whose namespace is represented by OrganizationClassificationSystem and value by OrganizationClassification.

Core.Person identifier architecture: PersonAlternateId and PersonIdSystem are superseded by PersonIdentification and PersonIdentificationSystem. Person identification now follows the same governed namespace/value pattern as organization identification.

FK metadata invariant: FKReference and Key must agree. A populated FKReference requires FK in Key; an FK marker requires an explicit target. Unambiguous identifier references must carry canonical FK metadata and target datatype. Recursive references to simple-key objects are explicit tenant-safe foreign keys. Version-sensitive parent references remain subject to the separate revision-specificity rule rather than being guessed.

The data model treats a CareerPathway as the overall route and CareerPathwayComponent as a step or element within that route. Job or occupation detail belongs to a component rather than acting as a separate peer target. Related facts point either to the whole pathway or to a specific component, not both levels at once.

The data model keeps occupation and industry classifications on the relevant job or occupation component rather than on the CareerPathway itself. The classification system is identified explicitly so the data model is not tied to a single taxonomy such as SOC, O*NET, OEWS, or NAICS.
The data model captures meaningful learner activity and progress measures. A streamed event may produce multiple measures, and each measure may retain a link to the source event that produced it.

The data model treats learner-success predictions as outputs from a defined prediction model rather than as a single generic success score. The prediction records the result for a learner at a point in time, while the model defines what is being predicted and how the result should be interpreted.

The data model uses one common PersonSupportReferral concept across advising, early alerts, challenges/intakes, and coordinated care rather than separate referral structures for each workflow. A referral identifies the person being supported, where they are being referred, and the resulting outcome.

The data model allows a support referral to be linked to the resulting participation in a resource or service, but the relationship is optional because a person may use a service without a formal referral.

The data model treats assessment and competency hierarchy as revision-specific. A revised assessment or competency may move to a different parent without changing the historical hierarchy of earlier revisions. Learning-resource parentage remains separate because “parent” can mean several different kinds of structure.

The data model records the actual occurrence time of time-sensitive student-support events rather than relying on record creation or source-import timestamps. This preserves meaningful chronology when data moves between systems.

The data model treats an OrganizationUnit as an internal unit of a specific organization within a tenant. TenantIdentifier establishes the data/security boundary, while OrganizationIdentifier identifies the organization that owns the unit.
